cards.text: In Proverbs, wisdom is pictured as a woman, and she is NOT using her inside voice. The teacher asks, 'Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?'

cards.question: Wisdom wants to be heard. Where does she take her stand to call out?

answers.text: At the crossroads and city gates

cards.text: Then wisdom starts talking: 'To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.' No guest list, no velvet rope, friend. She's calling out to EVERYBODY walking by.

cards.question: Wisdom calls out to the simple ones and to fools. What does she want them to do?

answers.text: Learn to be shrewd and gain understanding
Stay far away from the city gates
Keep quiet and let the wise speak

cards.text: Wisdom says, 'Listen, for I speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will reveal right.' Her mouth speaks the truth, and mine has said 'two more minutes' about the same batch for a WHOLE hour.

cards.question: True or false: wisdom says a few of her words are crooked, but most of them are righteous.
Wisdom says all her words are plain to the ___.

cards.text: Then wisdom makes an offer: 'Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.' Silver AND gold, and she says pass on it, friend, and the last time anybody put a price on ME, it was a sticker that said 25 cents.

cards.question: Why does wisdom say to choose her instruction over silver and gold?

answers.text: She is more precious than rubies
Silver and gold will rust away
Kings will reward them for it

cards.text: Wisdom introduces herself: 'I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.' Wisdom has roommates, friend.

cards.question: Wisdom explains what it means to fear the LORD. What does she say it is?
True or false: wisdom says she hates arrogant pride.

cards.text: Counsel, sound judgment, insight, strength: wisdom says it's ALL hers. She's not borrowing a single bit of it.

cards.question: Wisdom says that by her, ___ reign and rulers enact just laws.

cards.text: Princes rule by her too, and all nobles who govern justly. Then wisdom gets personal: she loves those who love her.

cards.question: True or false: wisdom says those who seek her early will find her.

cards.text: Wisdom says, 'With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.' And her fruit? Better than gold, pure gold, and her harvest beats choice silver.

cards.question: Wisdom walks in the way of righteousness and makes the ___ of those who love her full.

cards.text: Now wisdom takes us WAY back: 'The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.' That's not showing up early to work, friend. That's showing up before anybody built the OFFICE.

cards.question: Wisdom says she was established from the beginning, before the ___ began.

cards.text: No watery depths yet, no springs, no mountains, no hills, not even the dust of the earth. Wisdom was brought forth before ALL of it.

cards.question: True or false: wisdom says she was there when God established the heavens.

cards.text: She was there when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep, when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth. Front-row seat, friend.

cards.question: Then God turns to the sea. What does wisdom say He does with it?

answers.text: He sets a boundary for it

cards.text: The waters can't go past His command, and He marks out the foundations of the earth. Through all of it, wisdom says she was 'a skilled craftsman at His side'.

cards.question: Wisdom was a skilled craftsman at God's side. What does she say she was to Him day by day?
True or false: wisdom says she kept her distance from the sons of men.

cards.text: Now wisdom brings it home: 'Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.'

cards.question: Wisdom tells her listeners to listen to instruction and be wise. What does she tell them not to do with it?

cards.text: Then wisdom pictures the blessed man watching daily at her doors, waiting at the posts of her doorway. That's me EVERY single morning, nose pressed to the oven window, waiting on the first batch.

cards.question: Wisdom was the LORD's delight from the beginning. She says whoever finds her finds life and obtains the ___ of the LORD.
And the one who fails to find wisdom? What does she say he does?

cards.text: Then her last line: 'all who hate me love death.' Wisdom's been standing at the crossroads this whole time, friend, and she made the choice LOUD and clear.

findings.problem: The opening card says 'The teacher asks' but never says who the teacher is. It also doesn't say who wisdom is calling to. Proverbs never names a 'teacher' (that title belongs to Ecclesiastes), so the speaker of 8:1 is left unclear.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke is one long run-on sentence chained with 'and': 'Silver AND gold, and she says pass on it, friend, and the last time anybody put a price on ME, it was a sticker that said 25 cents.' It should be broken into short, punchy sentences.

This story card has three sentences: the quote line, 'That's not showing up early to work, friend.', and 'That's showing up before anybody built the OFFICE.' It isn't the passage's opening card, so the limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question's setup says 'Wisdom was the LORD's delight from the beginning.' 8:30 says she was His delight 'day by day' when He marked out the foundations of the earth. 'From the beginning' (8:23) describes when she was established, not her being His delight. The card joins the two and adds a time the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
